What's new in 0.13.0

  • **New pill type: Dial** — fire it and a small knob appears at your pointer; circle around it to turn the value notch by notch. Presets: Volume, Brightness, Keyboard Light, video Seek (←/→), arrow pairs — or record any two keys for the directions. Volume/brightness/keyboard-light dials show the live level as a number while turning; arrow dials show the arrow being pressed. Hold ⌥ while circling for fine steps. Each dial pill has its own sensitivity slider in its editor. The knob grows while you turn and shrinks when you stop; it starts with a little resistance from standstill (so drifting toward the centre never changes the value), ticks the trackpad on every notch, and closes on any click — which is swallowed, so nothing underneath gets clicked
  • **New menu: the Control Deck** — a ring of eight system dials (Volume · Brightness · Keyboard Light · Seek · Track · Zoom · Tabs · Spaces). Open it from the Compass's lower diagonal seat (its pill now shows a dial and says Controls), or from the new dial button in the arrange bar. Its pills are yours to edit and arrange like any menu
  • Compass: the two invisible diagonal seats (Settings, Controls) are marked with small dots that appear and leave with the menu; the Arrange seat is retired — arrange mode is the right-click on any centre hub
  • Arrow-key dials fire into the app the menu was opened over, not whatever app was focused
  • Settings side panel: opens over the same blur layer as the menu, and the blur sliders change the frost live while you drag — the Blur slider actually works now; sliders got a small dot that snaps back to the default when you drag near it; **Sound volume** moved from the menu-bar icon into the panel
  • Deleting a pill leaves its spot empty — the ring no longer slides everything over
  • Wide glyphs (tabs, spaces, play/pause and friends) are no longer shaved at the corners
  • Hotkey pills no longer go dead until you click into another app and back — the target window is given the keyboard before every send
  • The hub keeps leaning at a folder while it opens instead of snapping upright and back

What's new in 0.12.8

  • New pill options under **Switch**: Context · Shortcut · **System** — switch to an app and press one of the keyboard's own keys (Play/Pause, Next/Previous, Volume, Mute, Brightness, Keyboard Light, Apps, Mission Control)
  • The same keys are also available as plain **System** pills, without switching apps
  • The universal menu always opens on its **first** mode; hold ⌥ while opening (or while swiping to the Universal pill on the Compass — the pill flips to its second face) for the second mode
  • New in Settings → Feel: **Return pointer after firing** — after a pill fires, the pointer glides back to where you opened the menu (off by default)
  • Compass: after an unavailable menu springs back, nothing reacts until your hand is back at the centre — no accidental re-swaps on the way home
  • A folder closed by clicking it no longer reopens when you move back toward the centre — a pill only ever triggers on an inside-to-outside motion
  • Window pills act on the window you hovered only when it really is that window; a window opened a moment earlier no longer loses the command to an older one
  • Much smoother under the hand: everything that can appear during a gesture (toasts, the pill library, the arm indicator, the shortcut map, both settings surfaces) is pre-built at launch; the first open after launching — including the Compass — is pre-warmed; several background reads left the main thread

What's new in 0.12.7

  • Swipe open a folder and the pointer glides to the folder's centre — the same flight as after a Compass swap (clicking a folder open stays put)
  • The first menu open after launching or updating the app is warm — no cold stutter any more
  • Arrange mode: dropping a linked couple by its ⌥ lands it where you release it (it used to jump back to its old seat and slide over); dragging an ⌥ in a folder makes one sound, not two; no empty dashed box appears at the seat you are dragging a couple away from
  • Over the bare desktop, the hub shows Finder, and the arrange bar's context button arranges Finder's context menu (it showed the front app's pills under a Finder icon); Context/Window stay unavailable over the desktop as before
  • Compass aiming: nothing reacts until your hand is past the inner half of the hub, and tiny wobbles no longer re-aim at a neighbour
